correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening and upper selected San Diego Creek
correspondence.finding: The selection opens on the directly labelled San Diego Creek corridor near the State Highway 59 crossing and follows that creek southeast through the ranchland north of San Diego. Repeated labels and mapped intermittent channels, pool/wetland reaches and their joins support the entire selected upper corridor. This is a chosen point on the mapped creek, not a verified natural source.

correspondence.component_scope: San Diego Creek through San Diego and north of Alice
correspondence.finding: The mapped named creek continues through the San Diego town setting and east through the Muil/Springfield corridor to northern Alice. Its broad bends, incoming feeder channels and intervening joins correspond to the selection at ordinary corridor scale. The selected route does not require passage through the large Chiltipin reservoir north of Alice.

correspondence.component_scope: Chiltipin junction and short receiving San Fernando reach
correspondence.finding: The original maps show San Diego Creek meeting the Chiltipin Creek corridor northeast of Alice and a receiving channel directly labelled San Fernando Creek. The selection follows that short receiving reach before turning toward Pintas Creek. The nearby Chiltipin impoundment is on the incoming branch, rather than a selected lake-through passage. Exact name-boundary or confluence vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped San Fernando–Pintas side connection and upper Pintas corridor
correspondence.finding: The original depicts a blue channel linking the San Fernando corridor with the west end of the repeatedly labelled Pintas Creek corridor, followed by the eastward channel through the farmland south of Bentonville. This supplies ordinary mapped geographic correspondence for the selected transfer. Whether the connection is natural or managed, its flow direction under different conditions and any present operation are not established by this cartography; no such claim is imported from the unread CBBEP report.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle/lower Pintas Creek and Petronila junction
correspondence.finding: Repeated Pintas Creek labels follow the mapped eastward channel through the county-line and farm-road settings to its direct junction with Petronila Creek. The selected bends, incoming channels/ditches and this junction are supported at ordinary corridor scale. Agua Dulce Creek and Banquete Creek belong to the separate upstream Petronila approach and are not assigned to the selected Pintas path.

correspondence.component_scope: Petronila Creek from the Pintas junction past Driscoll
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns south along directly labelled Petronila Creek, passes the Lost Creek/La Paloma setting, crosses the highway at Driscoll and continues southeast. Repeated labels and the connected channel cover each selected part and intervening tributary/drainage join. Generalized bend clipping does not prevent this ordinary-scale correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Petronila, Gertrude-Lubby side lake and Chapman Ranch Lake settings
correspondence.finding: The named Petronila corridor continues southeast through its lower farm-country bends and past Gertrude-Lubby Lake and Chapman Ranch Lake. The maps show the lakes beside and connected to the creek corridor; the selected main route follows Petronila and is not relabelled as a lake chain. The lower joins and county-boundary passage are readable, without a material unseen interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Widening lower creek and Little Tule Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The labelled lower Petronila channel widens into the mapped Little Tule Lake estuarine reach. The selection follows this connected water corridor and continues to the receiving estuarine setting beside the arm labelled Cayo Del Mazon. The lake name and creek name have separate scopes; present tidal stage and the exact river-to-estuary boundary are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial part of the final estuarine segment
correspondence.finding: The beginning of the final part follows the connected estuarine water corridor beside Cayo Del Mazon. Cayo Hinosa is the spelling visible on the reference map farther south. These mapped named water settings provide regional context and local correspondence only; they do not establish the entire final diagonal extension.

correspondence.component_scope: Long final southeastward extension and actual selected ending
correspondence.finding: After the mapped estuarine corridor, the selected extension cuts southeast across intervening land/wetland east of the waterway, crosses the Cayo Hinosa water setting, and then crosses the land/wetland peninsula north of Alazan Bay. Its actual endpoint is in that peninsula setting rather than on a demonstrated continuous channel or an established creek mouth. The readable original does not supply a selected through-channel or a specified generalized aquatic connection across these land/wetland intervals. The broader connected estuary and nearby Alazan Bay name do not close this particular terminal gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern selected opening and initial westward-to-southwestern feeder
correspondence.finding: The original panels show the short westward upper arm and its southwestern continuation at the selected eastern opening. Figure 6b exposes the drainage beneath Figure 2’s geomorphological symbols. No separate hydronym is established for this initial feeder, and the Jungersen label is not imposed uniformly on it.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern southwestern sweep and southern bend
correspondence.finding: The thin mapped drainage follows the selected southwestern sweep, southern bend and beginning of the northwestern return. The intervening joins can be followed in Figure 6b and correspond to the same corridor in Figure 2. Nearby thematic glacial features are distinguished from the base hydrography.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern return and upper-middle westward continuation
correspondence.finding: The mapped northwestern return connects into the broader westward river corridor. The branch joins and transition into the middle valley are visible at ordinary corridor scale; no unshown cross-divide transfer is needed to connect these selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Jungersen River corridor and successive joins
correspondence.finding: The selected westward course corresponds to the continuous drainage labelled Jungersen River in the original maps. Neighboring northern and southern branches remain distinct. The mapped connections support representative identity without assigning the river name to every neighboring feeder or small waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower west-northwestward Jungersen corridor
correspondence.finding: The lower selected bends and short intervening joins follow the mapped Jungersen corridor toward the eastern shore of Jungersen Bay. The river label and the connected lower course agree in Figures 2 and 6b.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northwestern bends and Jungersen Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: The final mapped reach enters the southeastern/eastern end of Jungersen Bay, south of the separate Magda River outlet. The selected terminal corresponds to this river mouth at ordinary regional scale. The regional-setting prose independently states that Jungersen River drains into Jungersen Bay.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen_southwestern_opening_and_initial_turn
correspondence.finding: The supplied selected path begins with a short southeastern approach and a northward turn. This is orientation from the selected geometry only; no independent source map of the actual opening or its initial connection was read.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_northeastern_run_and_westward_turn
correspondence.finding: No independently read corridor-scale source establishes the selected upper northeastern run, its eastern turn, and subsequent western continuation. The path's position does not establish river identity or whether apparent joins traverse lakes or glacial terrain.

correspondence.component_scope: central_northwestern_continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected central parts and their intermediate joins lack independent cartographic correspondence. Regional coastal descriptions do not cover this inland interval.

correspondence.component_scope: western_middle_bend_and_northward_continuation
correspondence.finding: No source pixels establishing the selected westward bend, northward continuation, or their intervening waterbody/terrain passages were acquired. No flow or glacial classification is inferred from the selected line.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_northeastern_approach
correspondence.finding: The lower selected approach cannot be traced from the coast-focused ARC403 prose or its generalized chapter overview. A detailed independent source is still needed to distinguish the selected main channel and intervening joins.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_terminal_and_receiving_water
correspondence.finding: ARC403 Chapter10, printed page10-4, paragraphs51–54, identifies Richard Collinson Inlet between Barnard Point and Loch Point and describes a broad swampy head entered by a braided stream. That is geographically relevant coastal context, but the publication provides no readable detailed river map connecting the selected final two parts to a particular branch or naming that river. The receiving-water lead therefore remains unconfirmed for this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and initial easterly interval
correspondence.finding: The inspected teaching-book regional illustration and prose do not identify this opening as a named river or establish its initial channel continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: First northward turn and intervening easterly interval
correspondence.finding: No independently inspected detailed map or field description ties the selected northward turn and adjoining eastward segments into a named channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northern turn and northernmost easterly bend
correspondence.finding: The regional valley illustration locates several distinct Pampean valleys but cannot attribute this selected bend or its joins to one of their named rivers.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle eastward-to-southeast transfer
correspondence.finding: No actual source correspondence establishes the modeled transfer between the northern bend and lower southeastward corridor. Regional valley morphology is insufficient.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower east-southeast approach before the final turn
correspondence.finding: The book names several distinct regional salt lakes; it neither traces this approach into a particular lake nor supplies a river name for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southeast turn and actual inland endpoint
correspondence.finding: Colorada Grande is a documented salt-lake name in the regional literature actually read. No inspected usable terminal map establishes that the actual selected endpoint lies in that waterbody or connects to it along these final parts.
